messages.subject: Re: qtl for Mac OS X 10.3.x
messages.body_plain:
Try to download the file without unzipping it.  The file should be in
.tgz format, which you can install directly from R, clicking on
"Packages & Data" -> "Package Installer" -> "Local binary package".

Try downloading it directly from the following:

  http://www.biostat.jhsph.edu/~kbroman/software/qtl/qtl_0.98-57.tgz

karl

messages.subject: R/qtl version 0.99-22
messages.body_plain:
A new version of R/qtl (0.99-22) has finally been released at its web
site (http://www.biostat.jhsph.edu/~kbroman/qtl).  The Windows binary
will be posted tonight or tomorrow.

See http://www.biostat.jhsph.edu/~kbroman/qtl/STATUS.txt for a list of
changes.  Here are the major ones:

  scanone() now allows additive and interactive covariates in the
  case model="binary" (that is, for a binary trait).  This uses
  a logit link.

  scantwo() now allows analysis of binary traits (model="binary"),
  for method="em" only.

  Added a few new utility functions: bayesint() for calculating
  Bayesian probability intervals [cf lodint()], compareGeno for
  comparing individuals' genotypes, and strip.partials()
  for removing partially informative genotypes.

  Added +.scanone() and -.scanone() for adding and subtracting the
  output of scanone()

  Revised summary.scanone() and print.summary.scanone() so that it can
  summarize the result of multiple scanone() results together.

  Added code (the function sim.cc) for simulating the "Collaborative
  Cross" (8-way RILs) and for calculating QTL genotype probabilities
  and identifying the most likely genotypes (using Viterbi) with SNP
  data on such lines.

Karl Broman
